recent_posts.title: What It Means to Be a Forward Deployed AI Engineer
recent_posts.summary: A new hybrid role is emerging called the Forward Deployed AI Engineer, sitting between solutions engineer, staff developer, and product manager. The role involves rapid prototyping of LLM-backed pipelines from real customer workflows, live iteration with stakeholders, and then hardening those prototypes into production-grade systems with proper observability, evaluation, and guardrails — all under direct customer pressure.

recent_posts.title: Why I Built Octopal?
recent_posts.summary: Octopal is an AI agent framework built around an isolation-first security model. Instead of giving a single agent unrestricted access to the host machine, Octopal separates the planning brain (Octo) from action-taking workers that run in Docker containers by default. Workers only get access to the specific file paths they need, and their environments are deleted after completing tasks. This design reduces exposure to prompt injection, unsafe scripts, and other agent-targeting attacks. The post contrasts Octopal with OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, and NanoClaw, noting that while those tools support sandboxing, their defaults often allow host-side execution. Octopal includes memory, worker templates, channels, MCP, skills, recurring tasks, and a private gateway/dashboard in one runtime.

recent_posts.title: agentic-avatars
recent_posts.summary: A new NPM package called agentic-avatars provides zero-infrastructure, lip-synced 3D avatar components for AI voice agents. Built with React Three Fiber, it runs entirely in the browser and integrates with AI providers to add animated avatars to voice agent applications.

recent_posts.title: The Agent-Native IDP: How to Safely Give AI the Keys to Your Infrastructure
recent_posts.summary: Building an Agent-First Internal Developer Platform (IDP) requires treating AI agents as first-class citizens rather than bolting them onto legacy systems. The key architectural pillars are: controlled MCP server interfaces that enforce RBAC and governance boundaries, unified observability (OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Fluent Bit) for machine-consumable context, and declarative GitOps guardrails (Kubernetes, Argo Workflows, Flux) to catch and prevent hallucinated bad states. OpenChoreo, a recently released CNCF Sandbox project at v1.0.0, is presented as an open-source implementation of this pattern, shipping with built-in SRE and FinOps agents and secure MCP interfaces for custom agent integration.

recent_posts.title: Geolocating a Moving Bus From Window Photos — What AI Just Changed About OSINT
recent_posts.summary: Modern AI vision models have fundamentally changed OSINT geolocation by collapsing what once required expert skill into a seconds-long automated process. Three blurry photos from a moving bus were geolocated in under two minutes using an AI chatbot — no GPS metadata needed. The key shifts: the expertise barrier is gone, passive background details (signs, logos, architecture) are now locatable attack surfaces, aggregation of weak signals is automatic, and scale is trivially achievable. Stripping EXIF data is no longer sufficient privacy protection — the image content itself carries location information. The gap between 'a determined expert could figure this out' and 'anyone can do this instantly' is closing rapidly.

recent_posts.title: The "Vibe Coding" Reality Check: How to Actually Scale AI-Generated Apps
recent_posts.summary: Vibe coding with AI tools like Cursor or Copilot accelerates getting from 0 to 1, but creates serious infrastructure challenges when scaling AI-generated microservices. The core argument is that pairing GenAI with an Internal Developer Platform (IDP) is essential: AI should handle application logic while the platform manages Kubernetes configurations, GitOps pipelines, and observability. Three key infrastructure requirements are outlined: declarative platform abstractions as guardrails for AI-generated code, agent-ready design with native MCP server support, and opinionated golden-path workflows. OpenChoreo, a CNCF sandbox IDP, is highlighted as an example that treats AI agents as first-class citizens.

recent_posts.title: Stop Prompting: Use the Design-Log Method to Build Tools Predictably and Reliably
recent_posts.summary: The Design-Log Methodology addresses the 'context wall' problem in AI-assisted development by maintaining a version-controlled ./design-log/ folder with markdown documents capturing design decisions before any code is written. A practitioner shares how adopting this approach transformed their cybersecurity tool development workflow: instead of large prompts and back-and-forth corrections, they write a design log first, have the AI ask clarifying questions, freeze the design before implementation, and log any deviations. Four core rules guide the process: read before write, design before implement, immutable history, and Socratic questioning. The result is more reliable, auditable, and security-conscious AI-assisted development.

recent_posts.title: Top 5 Enterprise AI Gateways for Dynamic Routing in 2026
recent_posts.summary: A comparison of five enterprise AI gateways that support dynamic routing across multiple LLM providers. Covers Bifrost (Go-based, open-source, 11µs overhead), LiteLLM (Python, 100+ providers), Kong AI Gateway (plugin-based), Cloudflare AI Gateway (managed edge), and Azure API Management. Each is evaluated on routing features, strengths, and limitations. The core argument is that routing logic belongs in the infrastructure layer rather than application code.

recent_posts.title: How to Connect Non-Anthropic Models to Claude Code with a gateway
recent_posts.summary: Bifrost is an open-source Go-based LLM gateway that lets Claude Code route requests to non-Anthropic providers like OpenAI, Bedrock, Vertex AI, and Gemini. It exposes an Anthropic-compatible endpoint, requiring just one install command and one environment variable. Beyond routing, it offers automatic failover, a four-tier budget hierarchy, dual-layer semantic caching with Weaviate/Redis/Qdrant, and an MCP Code Mode that reduces token usage by over 50%. Benchmarks show 11 microsecond latency overhead and 5000 requests per second throughput. Best suited for teams with compliance requirements, multi-provider needs, or cost governance goals.

recent_posts.title: Local-first AI meeting copilot — 10 STT providers, 8 LLMs, zero cloud dependency
recent_posts.summary: NexQ is a local-first desktop meeting copilot built with Tauri 2 (Rust + React) that provides real-time transcription, translation, and AI assistance without any cloud dependency or bot joining your calls. It captures audio via WASAPI loopback, supports 10 STT providers including local Whisper, 8 LLM providers including local models via Ollama, and includes a local RAG pipeline for context-aware AI responses. The app features dual-party transcription, auto-detected questions and action items, past meeting review, and stores everything locally using SQLite. It's MIT licensed and fully configurable.
